Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
To maximise the satisfaction she derives from a given level of expenditure on two goods, X and Y, how should a consumer allocate her expenditure between the two goods?

options.A: marginal utility X = marginal utilityY
options.B: marginal utility X × price of X = marginal utility Y marginal utility X marginal utility Y
options.C: = price of Y price of X marginal utility X price of X
options.D: = marginal utility Y price of Y

questions.questionText: The line RS in the diagram is a consumer’s budget line. R N quantity of Y M S O quantity of X The consumer initially chooses the combination of X and Y indicated by point M on his budget line. He subsequently chooses the combination indicated by point N. What could explain the change from point M to point N?

options.A: a change in his tastes
options.B: a decrease in the price of X and a bigger percentage increase in the price of Y
options.C: an increase in the price of X and an increase in his income
options.D: equal percentage increases in his income and in both prices

options.A: a cut in the wage rate
options.B: a fall in the price of the final product
options.C: an increase in the wage rate
options.D: a rise in the price of the final product

A firm’s long-run production function shows that a 40% increase in its inputs leads to a 20% increase in output. What is the firm experiencing?

options.A: decreasing returns to scale

options.A: the law of variable proportions
options.B: the law of diminishing marginal utility

options.A: 32 units B 50 units C 64 units D 80 units

questions.questionText: What must a firm do to achieve internal growth?

options.A: increase productive capacity

An industry has an oligopolistic structure, but operates in a market which is highly contestable. What is most likely to result?

options.A: Collectively, the firms will behave like a monopoly.
options.B: Firms will earn normal profits in the long run.
options.C: Government price regulation will be required to prevent the exploitation of consumers.
options.D: There will be substantial barriers to the entry of new firms.

questions.questionText: What would economists agree should be the aim of any health care system?

options.A: to meet all the health care demands of the population
options.B: to provide every patient with the latest and best available treatment
options.D: to secure the maximum health gain from the resources available

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to give rise to a conflict between efficiency and equity?

options.A: an increase in government expenditure on health care
options.C: an increase in subsidies to public transport in congested urban areas
options.D: an increase in the highest rate of income tax

questions.questionText: Changes to a government’s welfare policies reduce the number of people who are eligible for welfare benefits. Why might these changes reduce income inequalities and the level of poverty?

options.A: Not everyone takes up the benefits for which they are eligible.
options.B: Some benefit recipients misspend the money they receive.
options.C: Those who lose their benefits will have a greater incentive to find employment.
options.D: Those who lose their benefits will pay less tax.

questions.questionText: What will expand the money supply in an open economy?

options.A: a current account balance of payments deficit
options.B: an increase in the cash reserve ratio of commercial banks
options.D: government intervention to prevent an appreciation in the foreign exchange value of domestic currency

What is likely to decrease a country’s actual output in the short run but may increase its long-run rate of growth of potential output?

options.A: a decrease in the proportion of 18-25 year olds in higher education
options.B: a decrease in the size of the government’s budget deficit
options.C: an increase in the size of the labour force
options.D: increased female participation in the labour force

questions.questionText: A fall in aggregate demand results in a rise in the number of full-time workers who are unemployed. What is the most likely direct consequence?

options.A: a deterioration in the country’s balance of trade
options.B: an influx of workers from abroad
options.C: a rise in the government’s budget deficit
options.D: a rise in the rate of inflation

options.A: a decrease in liquidity preference
options.B: a decrease in the level of national income
options.C: a decrease in the rate of investment
options.D: a decrease in the supply of money

questions.questionText: What could be expected to increase the pressure of demand-pull inflation in an open economy?

options.A: an appreciation of the foreign exchange rate
options.D: an increase in the budget deficit

questions.questionText: How might a developing economy gain from a multilateral reduction in import tariffs and the removal by developed economies of subsidies on food exports?

options.A: through increased specialisation leading to higher productivity
options.B: through increased ability to protect infant industries
options.C: through a reduction in the cost to the economy of imported food
